description: Adapted from vLLM's examples/observability/prometheus_grafana/grafana.json and the stat panels of examples/observability/dashboards/grafana/performance_statistics.json, at vLLM v0.30.0 (ced6857), Copyright contributors to the vLLM project, licensed under the Apache License 2.0: LICENSE-vllm.txt beside this file. Changed by simple-serving on 2026-09-27: the provisioned datasource; the model's names from vllm:num_requests_running; the observations beside every percentile; queue, prefill and decode times per request where upstream plotted rates of their sums; vLLM's waiting queue by reason; preemptions in place of the sequence group's maximum; a table over the whole range; and the descriptions. Every time here is vLLM's, not the gateway's or the reader's.

panels.description: vLLM's end-to-end request latency in seconds, from its arrival in vLLM to its end. vLLM's own time: it starts when vLLM's server takes the request from the gateway, after the gateway's wait for a count place, the count and the wait for a generation place, and it ends in vLLM. Neither the gateway's time nor the reader's (README, "Monitoring"). The bars on the right axis are the observations each percentile comes from, over the same window: a percentile of a handful says little.
panels.title: E2E Request Latency

panels.description: Prompt tokens vLLM processed (prefill) and tokens it generated, per second, all requests of every class together.
panels.title: Token Throughput

panels.description: Inter-token latency in seconds, measured between consecutive streamed outputs. It approximates TPOT when each output contains one token, but differs from request-level TPOT under speculative decoding or varying aggregation weights. With the drafter on, an output may carry several tokens. The bars on the right axis are the observations each percentile comes from, over the same window: a percentile of a handful says little. Here an observation is one interval, not one request.
panels.title: Inter Token Latency

panels.description: Requests in vLLM's running batches and in vLLM's own waiting queue, by reason as well: capacity waits for room in the batch or the KV cache. This queue is vLLM's, behind the gateway's own: a request in it already holds a gateway place. The gateway's queues are in the overview.
panels.title: Scheduler State

panels.description: vLLM's time to the first token, reasoning included, at P50, P90, P95 and P99. It leaves out the gateway's wait and count. vLLM's own time: it starts when vLLM's server takes the request from the gateway, after the gateway's wait for a count place, the count and the wait for a generation place, and it ends in vLLM. Neither the gateway's time nor the reader's (README, "Monitoring"). The bars on the right axis are the observations each percentile comes from, over the same window: a percentile of a handful says little.
panels.title: Time To First Token Latency

panels.description: The share of vLLM's KV cache blocks in use, 1 for all of them. When it runs full, vLLM preempts requests (below) and new ones wait in its queue.
panels.title: Cache Utilization

panels.description: Heatmap of request prompt length, in tokens, a request each as vLLM counted it.
panels.title: Request Prompt Length

panels.description: Heatmap of request generation length, in tokens, a request each as vLLM counted it.
panels.title: Request Generation Length

panels.description: Requests vLLM finished, by reason: stop, length, abort (the gateway closed the request: a client that left, a wall time, a drain), error or repetition.
panels.title: Finish Reason
Queue Time
panels.description: The time a request waited in vLLM's own queue before it was scheduled, at P50, P90 and P99, and its mean. Upstream plotted the rate of the sum, seconds of waiting per second. vLLM's own time: it starts when vLLM's server takes the request from the gateway, after the gateway's wait for a count place, the count and the wait for a generation place, and it ends in vLLM. Neither the gateway's time nor the reader's (README, "Monitoring"). The bars on the right axis are the observations each percentile comes from, over the same window: a percentile of a handful says little.

panels.title: Requests Prefill and Decode Time, mean per request
panels.description: The mean time a finished request spent in prefill, reading its prompt, and in decode, generating. Upstream plotted the rate of the sums. Preemption is inside both. vLLM's own time: it starts when vLLM's server takes the request from the gateway, after the gateway's wait for a count place, the count and the wait for a generation place, and it ends in vLLM. Neither the gateway's time nor the reader's (README, "Monitoring"). The bars on the right axis are the requests the means come from.

panels.title: Preemptions
panels.description: Requests vLLM took out of its running batch for lack of KV cache, per interval of the graph. A preempted request keeps its gateway place and continues later, so its wait shows in first_token_ms and total_ms. It replaces upstream's "Max Generation Token in Sequence Group": contract v2 refuses n > 1, so a group holds one request.

Per-request Time Per Output Token (TPOT) in seconds, computed as (end-to-end latency - TTFT) divided by the number of output tokens minus one. Requests with no more than one output token are recorded as zero; vllm bench serve excludes these requests from its TPOT statistics. The bars on the right axis are the observations each percentile comes from, over the same window: a percentile of a handful says little.
panels.title: Time Per Output Token (TPOT)
vLLM's times over the whole range
panels.description: P50, P90, P99 and the mean over the dashboard's whole range, each with the observations it comes from, adapted from the stat panels of vLLM's Performance Statistics dashboard. vLLM's own time: it starts when vLLM's server takes the request from the gateway, after the gateway's wait for a count place, the count and the wait for a generation place, and it ends in vLLM. Neither the gateway's time nor the reader's (README, "Monitoring").
